findings.title: Revisions are recorded after fn returns, so a checkpointed function that writes its own input in place yields a silently wrong gradient and the replay writes the caller's tensor a second time
findings.argument: The forward reads the input, fn bumps its revision, and the guard records the post-write revision; backward sees no change and replays fn on the written value. Check R1 case B on the shipped packages_r5 candidate: fn reads a=[1,2,3], then sets a[0]+=1 with mark_modified; b.grad is [2,2,3] (true [1,2,3]), no error, and a ends [3,2,3] because the replay repeats the write. The code comment and docstring assert the opposite ('fn's own in-place use of an input is part of the forward it saved'): checkpoint saves only the inputs, not their pre-fn values, so the replay cannot reproduce that forward. No test pins the timing (a mutant that records before fn passes all six tests), and r5m01 does not cover it. Not reachable in the R4a/R4b harness (segment inputs are fresh op outputs, and the F07 digest would flag it), but it is a silent-corruption path in the engine API.
findings.fix: Snapshot revisions before fn; after fn returns, raise at once if any changed ('checkpoint function modified input slot i in place'), or keep the pre-fn snapshot and refuse at backward. Fix the comment and docstring. Add case B as a host test and a mutant that records after fn.

findings.title: Tensors captured by fn's closure are outside the guard
findings.argument: Only the explicit input list is checked. Check R1 case C: w captured by the closure, changed with mark_modified after the forward; a.grad is [40,-5,6] (true [4,-5,6]), no error. The docstring says 'each input' and does not tell the caller that every tensor fn reads must be an input. The R4a harness passes all parameters explicitly and F12's census now refuses hidden containers, so it is not exposed.
findings.fix: Document the rule (every tensor fn reads must be passed as an input); optionally a debug mode that records the revisions of all leaves the forward touches.

findings.title: The checkpoint docstring's undetected-write list is narrower than attach_vjp's
findings.argument: attach_vjp's doc (bindings.cpp:2729-2732) also names writes through a DLPack re-import and APA packed_append. tc_signal's own untracked out= paths write through DLPack without mark_modified (_norms.py:111-115; __init__.py conv untracked paths), so a first-party API falls in the undetected class.
findings.fix: Copy attach_vjp's list into the checkpoint docstring and name tc_signal's out=.

findings.title: The zero/sign-flip power check cannot fail once the clean value passes
findings.argument: With bar rho*|fd|, rho<=1e-3: zeroing gives error |fd| > rho|fd|, and flipping gives about 2|fd|, for any fd != 0. So '18/18 power' restates 'clean passes and fd is nonzero'. The bar's real power is rho itself: it rejects any probe error above 0.1% (parameters) or 0.01% (style) of the probe value, against r4 candidate per-probe errors of at most 1.06e-4 relative.
findings.fix: None required; describe power as a property of the bar (smallest detectable relative error = rho).

findings.title: A3-1's floor never binds on the selected probes
findings.argument: Probes are the top-3 |g_ref| entries, so |fd|/(0.1*max|g|) is 6.8 to 10 on all 18 coordinate rows (REPORT_R5C table). The floor is a sanity check that fd is not noise. It cannot hide a defect: it is a validity rule, not acceptance; selection, seed and rho are unchanged; pass_fp64 is still required; no row was dropped. Registering it after the fp64-only data is a disclosed deviation with no candidate exposure.
findings.fix: None; state that it is non-binding by construction.

findings.title: A3-2 picks the step triple partly by agreement with the fp64 VJP
findings.argument: 'passes' includes max_error_ok against the VJP, so on the chosen row the FD is not independent of the VJP it checks. It is sound here: the plateaus 2.78e-4 / 6.95e-5 / 1.74e-5 for T(2)/T(1)/T(1/2) fall 4x per halving, the signature of O(h^2) truncation, and the chosen FD error 1.85e-5 is 300x below the candidate's rho*|fd| = 5.6e-3.
findings.fix: Choose by plateau among branch-free strong triples, then check max error separately.

findings.title: The replay-identity probe digests segment outputs only
findings.argument: Output identity per segment, with deterministic kernels and the F03 input guard, is strong evidence of exact recomputation. But an input change absorbed by rounding before the output would pass, and r5m02's kill depends on propagation. The r5m02 line requires the mismatch to land on the edited tag, so a non-propagating edit shows up as a survivor, never a false kill. The -0.0 delta is a valid single-element one-ulp mutant: x + (-0.0) is bitwise x for every x including +/-0, and the edit counts changed elements and refuses anything other than one.
findings.fix: Also digest each segment's replay inputs against its forward inputs.

findings.title: The suite-gpu line's 'no GPU test may skip' rule is name-based
findings.argument: It flags skips only when '::test_gpu' is in the ID. tensor_cuda/tests/test_bwd_r1_core.py has four @gpu tests named test_core_* (test_core_matmul_geometries x5, test_core_leaky_ties x3, test_core_maximum_first_slot_on_equality, test_core_matmul_exact_cancellation_and_zero_taps); their skips would not fail the line.
findings.fix: Fail on any skip on the GPU line, or on any skip whose reason names CUDA.

findings.title: The misleading R4_G1 worst_parameter line is still emitted
findings.argument: g1_annotated calls gate.comparison, which still picks the worst relative L2 over floor rows (r4: 7.9e8 on a zero-gradient bias). The correct worst lives in G1_GROUPS.
findings.fix: Relabel or drop that field in the old summary.

findings.title: G5's figure is called an upper bound on this process's use
findings.argument: It bounds the process's use only at the sampled instants; unsampled transients can exceed it, as the same note says NVML would catch.
findings.fix: Say 'upper bound at the sampled phases'.
